ISSUE 007
THU AUG 20 2026
The Nashville stuff that’s here for a moment, then gone.
Food, drink, and the cool stuff to do — ranked by how little time you’ve got left to catch it.
The CountdownHappening now
Short windows landing this week — here and then gone.
Closes Sunday, Aug 23Event
An American Story: Paintings from the Parthenon's Cowan Collection
Cheekwood, Belle Meade

Fifty-seven American painters, gifted to the city a century ago, and out of the Parthenon for the first time in nearly forty years. It goes back behind the columns on Sunday. Four days left on a forty-year window.

See it before it goes back →
Sat Aug 22, 4-9 PMFood + Drink
25th Annual Music City Brewers Fest
Walk of Fame Park, Downtown

Forty-plus breweries pouring in one park for the twenty-fifth year, with a mechanical bull and food trucks between tastings. VIP gets in at four, general at five, and the whole thing benefits Nashville Humane. When the taps close, that's the year.

Grab a pour →
Last day Sat Aug 22Event
Wilson County - Tennessee State Fair
Lebanon

Ten days of livestock, refurbished rides and fried everything, and Saturday is the end of it. Funnel cake has a season and the season ends this weekend.

Go before it packs up →
Sat Aug 22, 10 AM-12 PM, $40 for twoFood + Drink
Wild About Fungus
Owl's Hill Nature Sanctuary, Brentwood

Learn to grow oyster mushrooms, build a grow kit to take home, then walk the sanctuary identifying what is already out there. Forty dollars covers two people and the kit. Pre-registration only, and it is Saturday.

Take the class →
Fri-Sat Aug 21-22, $65 weekend passFilm
Defy Film Festival
East Side Bowl, East Nashville

Eleventh year of an independent film festival held in a bowling alley, which is the most East Nashville sentence in this issue. Two days, unlimited screenings on the weekend pass, then it's gone for a year.

Get the weekend pass →
Fri-Sat Aug 21-22, 7 PM, from $65Music
Songwriters Under the Stars
Swan Lawn at Cheekwood, Belle Meade

GRAMMY-winning hitmaker Chris DeStefano and The Warren Brothers trade the stories behind the hits, with the Music City Symphony behind them and a tribute to Brett James in the middle of it. Lawn seating, food trucks, two nights, done. Pair it with the Cowan paintings and make one trip.

Get on the lawn →
Fri-Sat Aug 22-23, 8 PMMusic
Big Thief at the Ryman
Ryman Auditorium, Downtown

Two nights at the Mother Church for the band that makes a room go quiet on purpose. Adrianne Lenker's voice in that hall is the argument for the Ryman existing. Two dates, no third.

Get in the pews →
The Ryman, This FortnightJust surfaced
The next two weeks, before they’re gone.
Thu Aug 27, 7:15 PMEvent
Chromatic & Friends MYSTERY Pop-Up Show
Berry Hill

The lineup is the secret. Chromatic brings unnamed special guests to a small Berry Hill room and you find out who when you walk in. A format that only works once, which is why it only happens once.

Take the gamble →
Fri Aug 28, 12-2 PMFood + Drink
Cast Iron Master Class Lunch at Yolan
The Joseph, Downtown

Chef de Cuisine Liam Byres runs a two-hour lunch built entirely around cast iron - seasoning it, cooking in it, eating out of it - to mark The Joseph's sixth, the iron anniversary. One seating, inside a kitchen that does not usually let you watch.

Book the seat →
Fri Aug 28, 5-10 PM, $43, 18+Event
Adults Only Night at The Adventure Park
Belle Meade

A hundred and sixty treetop platforms and thirty-one zip lines, lit up after dark, with the under-eighteens sent home. Five hours of having the forest to yourselves, for forty-three dollars.

Climb after dark →
Mon Aug 24Food + Drink
Big Table: Eats Around the World
Franklin Marriott Cool Springs

A chef-driven trip through Morocco and Brazil for one night, with live music and a live auction, and every dollar going to hospitality workers in crisis. The city's cooks feeding the city's cooks.

Take a seat at the table →
Fri-Sun Aug 28-30, almost sold outFood + Drink
Nashville Eats & Beats Festival
The Fairgrounds, Melrose

Three days of vendors and live sets at the Fairgrounds - the kind of graze where you eat standing up and stay for the band anyway. The listing already reads almost full, which is the part that should move you.

Get in while there are tickets →
On a TimerSeasonal
Here now, gone when summer is.
Through Labor Day, Sep 7Food + Drink
Capricious - the Fairlane rooftop pop-up bar
Fairlane Hotel, Downtown

The Fairlane turned its rooftop into the Italian coast for the season - fourteen-dollar Aperol spritzes, a six-pour spritz tower, the whole Capri bit above Union Street. It runs to Labor Day and not one day past it.

Go while it's warm →
One Night OnlyTicketed
Seated and finite. When it sells, it’s done.
Tue Sep 15, 6:30 PMFood + Drink
Duckhorn Wine Dinner at Char
Char, Green Hills

Five courses, each poured against a Duckhorn Vineyards wine, at one of the better steakhouses in town. One seating, one night, and the sort of Tuesday that quietly fills up before anyone announces it did.

Take a seat →
Sep 4-6, on sale nowMusic
Music City Underground
The Pinnacle, Downtown

Deep Tropics takes over The Pinnacle for three days of global electronic - house, techno, bass - across two immersive stages, floor to roof. One weekend a year, and this year it has a name.

Get the wristband →
Sat Aug 29, 7 PMEvent
Please Don't Destroy LIVE
Polk Theater at TPAC, Downtown

The three SNL writers behind "Three Sad Virgins" take the sketch off the screen and into the Polk for one night. The bit does not survive being watched later on a phone, which is the entire argument for going.

Get a seat →
On the CalendarPlan ahead
The big ones worth planning for — so you never get caught missing it again.
Sat Sep 5, 7:30 PM, freeMusic
American Mosaic: A Free Community Concert
Walk of Fame Park, Downtown

Leonard Slatkin conducts, Gary Sinise narrates, and 4K footage from all fifty states runs behind the orchestra - plus Copland's Fanfare and Stars and Stripes to close out Labor Day weekend. Free, outdoors, bring a blanket.

Put it on the calendar →
Sep 25-27, free, opens Fri 11 AMEvent
Artville
Walk of Fame Park, Downtown

Seventy-five contemporary craft and fine artists take over the park across from the Hall of Fame for three days, free, with site-specific installations, live music and food. Worth planning around.

Mark the weekend →
